articles.title: The Witcher is a perfect fit for Reigns’ Tinder-like roleplaying
articles.summary: In Reigns: The Witcher, the team at Nerial and Devolver Digital have turned the fantasy into a Tinder-like adventure on Steam, the iPhone, and Android.
articles.body: I never knew how easy it was to die in an orgy. But that’s just one of the many threats facing Geralt of Rivia in his latest adventure. The studio behind the Reigns series of Tinder-like choose-your-own-adventure games has now adapted The Witcher, following a handful of original titles and a take on Game of Thrones. And for Francois Alliot, creative director at Reigns studio Nerial, the series’ structure actually makes it an ideal way to ease players into sprawling fantasies like this. “There’s something about the way you can bring really complex universes, lore, and storylines to simple actions,” he says. “It can work in a lot of contexts.” What makes Reigns so approachable is the way it distills every action into a binary choice. As you play, you’re presented with cards, and you progress by either swiping right or left. In the case of The Witcher, for instance, an elf might ask Geralt for protection, and your options are simply to say either yes or no and then deal with the consequences. Each run through the game involves making a number of these decisions to progress a storyline until, well, you die. [Media: The idea was for Reigns: The Witcher to work on two levels. For existing fans, it’s a fun way to play around and experiment in the world. “It’s not a new Witcher,” Alliot notes. “It’s a meta game around this universe, a bit like a fanfiction simulator.” But for those who might be intimidated by the franchise, which spans multiple books, games, and TV shows, it’s also a good place to start. “It works nicely as an entry point because you can really get a feel for the tone and rules, or lack of rules, of the world,” says narrative designer Oscar Harrington-Shaw. “But you’re not having to commit to a complex RPG.” There are several aspects of the Reigns formula that had to be tweaked to work with The Witcher. One of the key conceits in the games is that you can die; in the original Reigns you played as a king, and when that was over you picked up as their successor. But that doesn’t really work when you’re playing a character like Geralt who can’t die. So you aren’t actually playing as Geralt; instead, you’re his bard pal Dandelion, singing tales of Geralt’s exploits that may or may not be true. This allowed the team at Nerial to “free ourselves from the lore,” as Alliot describes it, and have fun with things. This is especially apparent in the deaths, which come in the form of the aforementioned orgies or even from Geralt drinking himself to an early grave. “It really helped in two ways,” Harrington-Shaw says of coming up with the Dandelion idea, which came about from discussions with Witcher studio CD Projekt Red. “One is that it helps explain the loop; it gives a really neat end point. And we can have loads of fun deaths because it’s just a satisfying ending to a song. But we think it adds a really fun tension because you are playing as Geralt and you’re trying to survive, but you’re also trying to write good content.” [Image: As I played, this setup made me much more open to experimenting. Instead of trying to roleplay as Geralt, I would often make odd choices just to see what happened. This, in turn, helps open up new storylines, giving some payoff for making the seemingly wrong decision. Even an early death can lead somewhere interesting in future runs. The other notable addition in Reigns: The Witcher is a combat system. It wouldn’t be The Witcher if Geralt wasn’t slaying some monsters, but the idea of battles also had the potential to complicate the streamlined Reigns structure. The team settled on a sort of rhythm game, where you’re moving Geralt side to side on a board to attack or avoid monsters. What makes this system work within the confines of Reigns is that you’re still using the same commands; whether you’re making a pivotal decision or staring down a striga, everything comes down to swiping either right or left. Despite those changes, Harrington-Shaw says that The Witcher universe is an almost ideal fit for Reigns thanks to its dark sense of humor and frequently bleak world full of opposing factions. More important, though, is the main witcher himself. “Geralt is always facing these tricky binary choices,” he says. “The world of The Witcher is full of murky, gray morality, and that seemed perfect to translate.” Reigns: The Witcher is out now on PC and mobile.

articles.title: 007 First Light is like a James Bond movie in the best way possible
articles.summary: With the James Bond game 007 First Light, Hitman developer IO Interactive has crafted an interactive Bond film.
articles.body: The James Bond franchise is nothing if not a spectacle: Aside from the explosions and gunfights, even its calmer moments are dripping in the pomp and glamour of elite ostentation and luxury locales. Bond, however, has always been an odd mascot for the espionage profession, which ordinarily operates under silence and shadows. With 007 First Light, an origin story from Hitman developer IO Interactive, that spectacle rivals any of Bond’s cinematic adventures. Across 20 some hours with the game, those moments punctuated one of my favorite action games in years, one filled with exhilarating combat and an incredible variety of missions. The game starts with Bond, still merely a British soldier, called in with his squad to check in on unresponsive scientists operating in the frozen wilderness of Iceland. The squad is shot down and only Bond survives. The opening sequence is, unfortunately, extremely generic, but it does its job in setting up Bond’s future. Despite the improbable odds, he succeeds, but not without killing several bad guys and blowing things up. It’s this, combined with his refusal to leave people to their fate, that garners the attention of “M,” the new head of the reinstated “00” program of MI6 (the United Kingdom’s foreign intelligence service). Bond joins the recruitment program and starts training, under the guidance of the irascible Greenway, played by The Walking Dead’s Lennie James. To say more would spoil the otherwise enjoyable plot, but the story explores everything from double agents to the rise of AI and corporate control of humanity. Don’t let his recruit status fool you: This is James Bond. He is charming, funny, an incredible fighter, highly intelligent, and surprisingly emotional and caring. No doubt much was drawn from Daniel Craig’s turn as the character, though there is no relation to the films. More importantly, playing as Bond feels incredible, as he is highly responsive, agile, and adaptive. In melee fights, he’ll not merely punch and kick when you press the “hit” button, he will also throw enemies headfirst into walls and windows if they are nearby; he will grab smashable objects to destroy on their heads; he will charge them. First Light is powered by the Glacier engine, the same tech behind the Hitman series, creating an ultrarealistic environment with breakable objects and interiors; papers fly, smoke lingers, objects spin and roll. Like Bond himself, the environment is incredibly responsive. [Media: What really makes First Light work is the variety in missions. We go from tracking government workers in underground London nightclubs to a sprawling, multilevel Slovakian castle hosting a major chess match to uncover a double agent. And, in keeping with Bond tradition, each mission escalates, often in unexpected ways. At one point, Bond engages in a car chase that ends up chasing down and destroying a plane; another mission has you navigating a pirate den in a fictional Mauritanian city, having to raise $100,000 by participating in a range of illegal activities, from fistfights to gambling. I should note that the pirate den is where you meet Bawma, played by Lenny Kravitz. Oddly, he’s being touted by some places as the main antagonist, when he is not only not a villain, let alone the main villain, but also has a total screentime of about five minutes. It’s not a huge loss, though: Kravitz’s performance is terrible, and his American accent jarring. Though it comes from the team that made Hitman, I very rarely had to wear disguises or deceive my way into places — a frequent occurrence in Hitman that would also make a lot of sense for an espionage game. Instead, Bond finds other methods, usually grates and sewers, to enter spaces. I used disguises twice in my entire playthrough. Stealth is still your primary method of approach, but there is no insta-fail state. Bond can make quick work of multiple enemies, but it felt “wrong” to me when I failed stealth. If, like me, you choose to load a checkpoint to keep your stealth streak, be prepared for strangely long loading times and very annoying checkpointing. I couldn’t tell if IO even wanted me to focus on stealth, given the checkpoints before long unskippable conversations or before extensive platforming sections. [Image: Before every mission, like in the films, Bond is kitted out by Q, the head of research at MI6 headquarters. Here, you can also speak to colleagues, hear conversations about your missions, and so on. It made MI6 not merely a faceless entity but alive with people you come to know. This becomes important for later developments I’d rather not spoil. You can take at most three devices into each mission, ranging from the laser watch to nausea darts. Every device is useful. Padlock on a door? Laser it. A guard is blocking a hallway? Shoot him with a nausea dart. Your choices directly impact how you’re able to approach situations in the field. During missions, you will encounter various “opportunities,” which make a return from Hitman. You may overhear a conversation about a reporter running late, then assume his identity to get into restricted areas; one time, I managed to fleece an ID card off a man all because I overheard his friend’s name. First Light’s variety kept me on my toes, never once allowing me to guess where the game would go. The spectacle and set pieces rival even Uncharted, without ever once making me feel like I was merely a spectator. It’s not the Hitman-like game I initially expected given its developer; instead, it’s one of the best action games I’ve ever played, one that leans into the elements that have made Bond so enduring. And with the future of the film franchise up in the air, First Light is coming at exactly the right time and clearly in the right hands. 007 First Light launches on the PC, PS5, and Xbox on May 27th; a Switch 2 version is also in the works.

articles.title: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt’s Daughter Zahara Becomes Their Third Child to Officially Drop Pitt from Last Name
articles.summary: Four of the six children Jolie and Pitt share have petitioned to change their last name to “Jolie” rather than “Jolie-Pitt”
articles.body:
A judge has approved a name change petition from Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie's daughter Zahara

As of Sept. 28, the former couple's eldest daughter now goes by "Zahara Marley Jolie" rather than "Zahara Marley Jolie-Pitt," according to court records obtained by PEOPLE

Four of Pitt and Jolie's six children have made the legal move to drop Pitt from their last names, with Shiloh, Maddox and Zahara getting legal approval, while Vivienne awaits her court hearing

Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie 's daughter Zahara has officially dropped her father's last name.

As of her name change petition hearing on Monday, Sept. 28, Zahara, 21, now goes by "Zahara Marley Jolie" rather than "Zahara Marley Jolie-Pitt." Court filings obtained by PEOPLE show a California judge approved the change with no objections.

Pitt, 62, and Angelina, 51, share six children : Maddox , 25, Pax , 22, Zahara, Shiloh , 20, and twins Vivienne and Knox , 18. The Mr. and Mrs. Smith stars separated in 2016 after 12 years together and two years of marriage, finalizing their divorce in December 2024.

Zahara petitioned to have "Pitt" removed from her last name on June 9 in a filing that dated back to April 28. Days earlier, Maddox also filed to remove his father's last name. In July, both siblings confirmed their intent by publishing legal notices in the Los Angeles Daily Journal in accordance with California law.

On Sept. 14, Maddox's name change from "Maddox Chivan Jolie-Pitt" to "Maddox Chivan Jolie" became official , according to public court records reviewed by PEOPLE.

The move came exactly 10 years after an alleged incident involving Pitt and his family on a private plane ride. Sources previously laimed that on Sept. 14, 2016, the Oscar winner allegedly was "verbally abusive" and "physical" with one of his kids. (While Pitt was under investigation on suspicion of child abuse , the FBI later cleared the Ocean's star, while the L.A. County Department of Children and Family Services concluded its investigation with no findings of abuse .)

Maddox and Zahara have followed the legal move from Shiloh, who filed to drop Pitt's name on her 18th birthday back in 2024.

On her own 18th birthday this past July, Vivienne filed to change her name from "Vivienne Marcheline Jolie-Pitt" to "Vivienne Marcheline Jolie." Following another publication in the Los Angeles Daily Journal , her name change petition court hearing is set for Nov. 2.

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

In July 2024, a source close to Pitt told PEOPLE that the F1 actor-producer had "virtually no contact" with his adult children , but still had visitation with his younger kids at the time. Earlier this month, a source confirmed to PEOPLE that "there's very little communication right now" between Pitt and his children, calling the situation "a tragedy."

"This is the result of a prolonged campaign of alienation of children against their parent," the source told PEOPLE . "It's an incredibly sad reality, but it's not surprising after years of one parent weaponizing the children against the other one with no regard for the consequence."

Zahara had previously hinted at her name change. When she walked the stage during her graduation from Spelman College in Atlanta in May, her name was read as "Zahara Marley Jolie," and she introduced herself as such in a speech while joining the Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority in November 2023.

A source told PEOPLE in May that Jolie has an "amazing relationship" with her daughter , and that the actress-activist shows up for "pretty much everything" Zahara is involved in.

"She really encourages all the kids to embrace their individualities. She always loved their different personalities, interests and talents," the insider added. "She makes an effort to support what matters to each of them."

articles.title: Cronos do Venom: morre Conrad Lant, vocalista da banda, aos 63 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: 'Por mais de quatro décadas, a voz, o baixo e a visão de Conrad foram o coração do Venom', afirmou banda de heavy metal. Causa da morte não foi divulgada.
articles.summary: Cronos do Venom, pioneiro do metal extremo, faleceu nesta quinta-feira; banda lamentou a perda do músico que transformou o gênero por quatro décadas.
articles.body:
Conrad 'Cronos' Lant, vocalista do Venom, — Foto: Stefan Johansson/Divulgação

Conrad "Cronos" Lant, vocalista e baixista da banda de heavy metal britânica Venom, morreu aos 63 anos, de acordo com anúncio do grupo nesta quinta-feira (1º). A causa da morte não foi divulgada.

"Por mais de quatro décadas, a voz, o baixo e a visão de Conrad foram o coração do Venom", escreveu a banda, no Instagram.

"Ele criou algo que mudou a música pesada para sempre. Venom nunca seguiu as regras. Eles construíram o próprio caminho. E Conrad estava lá, no centro de tudo — intransigente, destemido e inconfundível."

Formado na Inglaterra, em 1978, o Venom se tornou um dos mais influentes nomes do thrash metal e do black metal — tanto que seu segundo disco, "Black metal", deu o nome do subgênero — no começo dos anos 1980.

"Gostaria de agradecer a todas as Legiões por todo o apoio que deram ao meu pai ao longo dos anos. Eu sei que ele gostava demais de todos vocês", afirmou o filho de Conrad, Nathan. "Ele descansou sua alma, e sua música continuará viva. A lenda de Cronos nunca morrerá."

articles.title: Jim Carrey marries girlfriend Min Ah in private ceremony
articles.summary: The two have been spotted together as far back as 2022, but Carrey kept details of their relationship under wraps.
articles.body:
Jim Carrey recently married his girlfriend Min Ah in a private ceremony.

The couple has been spotted together as far back as 2022, but details of their relationship remain scarce.

Carrey has been married twice, shares one child with ex Melissa Womer, and has dated Linda Ronstadt, Renée Zellweger, January Jones, and Jenny McCarthy.

Congratulations are in order for Jim Carrey , who has married Min Ah.

The Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind star, 64, and his girlfriend recently tied the knot, his rep confirmed to Entertainment Weekly . TMZ reports that they swapped vows in a small, private ceremony in Los Angeles.

He and Ah made their official debut as a couple on Feb. 26 at the César Awards in Paris, where he was also alongside his adult daughter, Jane, and her teenage son, Jackson.

When the Ace Ventura: Pet Detective star received an honorary award, he made sure to shout out Ah during the speech he gave in French, per PEOPLE .

"Thank you to my wonderful family, my daughter Jane, and my grandson Jackson. I love you now and forever," the actor said through translation. "Thank you to my sublime companion, Min Ah," he said in French, as his daughter, grandson, and girlfriend received ovations from the crowd. "I love you, Min Ah. And finally, thank you to the funniest man I have ever known: my father, Percy Joseph Carrey who taught me the value of love, generosity, and laughter."

Carrey and Ah were first photographed together in 2022.

The actor has been married twice before. He and Melissa Womer, with whom he shares Jane, were married from 1987 to 1995. In 1996, Carrey married Dumb and Dumber costar Lauren Holly, but they split the following year.

Carrey has also had relationships with famous women including Jenny McCarthy, Renée Zellweger, Linda Ronstadt, and January Jones.

The union with Ah was consummated despite Carrey's insistence that he wouldn't walk down the aisle again.

He said it in a March 2008 interview with Britain's Weekend Magazine : "I'm happy with Jenny," Carrey said of McCarthy. "Although I probably won't get married again. If you've done it twice, you really should stop doing it."

He confirmed his stance on Howard Stern's SiriusXM radio show in 2014.

"I just don't see it as necessary, at this point," Carrey said. "I can't say that I know how I would feel if I meet somebody that knocks my head off. I mean, I can't make hard, fast rules about the future. But I wouldn't voluntarily go that way."

Looks like his "sublime companion" changed his mind.

articles.title: 'How can they break the FDs?': Upasana Singh alleges CINTAA’s Rs 90 lakh FDs lakh fixed deposits were accessed without consent, names Poonam Dhillon and Padmini Kolhapure
articles.summary: The ongoing dispute over the management of the Cine and Television Artistes’ Association (CINTAA) has taken another turn, with former office-bearer
articles.body: The ongoing dispute over the management of the Cine and Television Artistes’ Association (CINTAA) has taken another turn, with former office-bearer Upasana Singh making fresh allegations over the organisation’s bank accounts and fixed deposits. Singh has claimed that funds belonging to CINTAA were transferred after an account that had allegedly been frozen was accessed. She has also questioned how the association’s fixed deposits could have been withdrawn without members being consulted.Upasana Singh alleges CINTAA account was accessed after being frozenAccording to IANS, in an exclusive conversation with the news agency, Upasana Singh claimed that CINTAA has bank accounts and fixed deposits across five banks. She alleged that the banks had been informed about the dissolution of the previous committee and were asked to keep the accounts frozen until a new committee formally took charge.“We have FDs in five banks and accounts in five banks. When our committee was dissolved, Deepak Parashar was the treasurer. So, we informed all the banks that the committee had been dissolved. We told them that when a new committee comes, whoever takes charge, the accounts can be opened. Until then, they should remain frozen,” Upasana Singh told IANS.She said the understanding was that the accounts would become operational only after the legal status of the new committee was established.According to Singh, the issue came to light after the committee believed it had secured a recent victory and planned to approach the banks again. She alleged that the account had already been accessed before the banks were formally informed about the new committee.“When we won a few days ago, we thought we would again inform them that this committee has come in. But our understanding was that the accounts would be opened only after a court order came stating that this committee would now function. Until then, they should not be opened,” she said.Singh further alleged that money from CINTAA’s fixed deposits had been transferred after the account was accessed.“We found out that the account had already been opened. They had opened their account there, and the money from CINTAA’s FDs was transferred into it. They have used that money in different places,” she alleged.Upasana Singh questions how CINTAA’s FDs could be brokenSingh also questioned the procedure allegedly followed to access CINTAA’s fixed deposits. She argued that members should have been consulted before the association’s funds were withdrawn.“It is such a big issue because if you want to break the FDs of any institution, you have to ask the members first. How can they break the FDs?” she said.When asked whether an authorised signature would have been required to carry out such a transaction, Singh alleged that office staff helped facilitate access to the account.“They must have needed an authorised signature. But you see, the account was frozen. So what did they do? They met the office staff. The office staff is involved with them. They took the staff to the bank and showed them the stamp, the email ID and the office, and asked them to open the account through KYC,” she alleged.Upasana Singh names Poonam Dhillon and Padmini KolhapureWhile recounting what she alleged happened at the bank, Singh specifically named actors Poonam Dhillon and Padmini Kolhapure, besides Paintal.“They took Paintal saab, Poonam and Padmini and told the bank, ‘This is our stamp, this is our email ID and this is our office. You open our account through KYC.’ The staff was also there and showed the bank that this was their office,” she claimed.Singh also questioned whether those involved had the authority to represent themselves as CINTAA office-bearers.“When you are not holding any position and you are not the general secretary, how can you say that you are the general secretary? They declared themselves as the committee,” Upasana alleged.CINTAA has around Rs 90 lakh in FDs, claims Upasana SinghSingh said the alleged movement of funds took place through multiple transactions and that the exact number of fixed deposits that may have been accessed was not yet known.“The money was transferred in different ways. We don't know how many FDs have been broken because we have around Rs 90 lakh there,” she told IANS.The allegation comes amid a wider dispute over CINTAA’s administration and competing claims surrounding the association’s committee and control of its financial accounts. The controversy has previously involved allegations over frozen bank accounts and the functioning of the association.Poonam Dhillon and Padmini Kolhapure have previously rejected allegationsThe latest allegations should be viewed in the context of the ongoing CINTAA dispute. Poonam Dhillon and Padmini Kolhapure have previously publicly disputed allegations made by Singh and other former members. In an August press interaction, the two addressed accusations concerning CINTAA’s functioning and finances, with Dhillon denying wrongdoing and Kolhapure also rejecting the claims. In September, Dhillon and Kolhapure also spoke publicly about CINTAA’s frozen accounts, alleging that the freezing had affected the association’s welfare activities and staff payments.As of the latest IANS report on October 1, 2026, there was no response from Dhillon or Kolhapure specifically addressing Singh’s fresh allegations about the alleged breaking of the FDs. articles.title: Diego Luna se lo deja muy claro a Broncano: "Es mentira, como todo lo que se dice en este programa"
articles.standfirst: El actor responde de manera directa al presentador en ‘La Revuelta’
articles.summary: El actor responde de manera directa al presentador en ‘La Revuelta’
articles.body: El pasado miércoles, 30 de septiembre, el programa ‘La Revuelta’ tuvo al actor Diego Luna como invitado ilustre y que llegaba al plató para promocionar su nueva película: ‘Ceniza en la boca’. Durante su entrevista, y ante una de las peticiones más habituales de David Broncano, el intérprete no dudó en responder de forma brusca al jienense y provocar un momento de desconcierto. Broncano quiso conocer el tiempo de uso del móvil de Diego Luna, pero este quiso ver qué tocaba el presentador del espacio de entretenimiento y comprobar que no accediera a otras aplicaciones. “Vaya dato, duro”, avisó el comunicador. Mientras, el actor aclaró que el día anterior, por ejemplo, vio una película mientras viajaba de Pamplona a Alicante. “Nunca había visto eso”, expresó Luna al ver la pantalla, pero Broncano ya dejaba claro que el dato era especialmente alto: “O la película duraba ocho horas…”. El jienense acabó revelando que durante las últimas 24 horas el invitado había usado su smartphone durante 11 de ellas. “No juzgo”, dijo Broncano cuando Diego Luna trataba de contar que él trabaja con el móvil. “Hace un rato me estabas abrazando, ahora me estás viendo como mi tía”, bromeó el actor, que respondió de forma tajante cuando Broncano le pidió que contara qué le iba a decir a sus hijos cuando vieran la emisión. “Que es una mentira, como todo lo que se dice en este programa”, manifestó en tono de broma Diego Luna. El intérprete saltó a la fama mundial en 2018 con el estreno de ‘Narcos: México’, una de las series de mayor éxito en Netflix. Además, se unió al universo de Star Wars, llegando a protagonizar la serie ‘Andor’ en 2022, con dos temporadas de mucho apoyo en Disney+ y con una buena crítica a nivel mundial.

articles.title: La petición de Marc Giró, presentador, a Pedro Sánchez: "Cuanto más cabreado tengas a Felipe González, muchísimo mejor"
articles.standfirst: Entre risas y sátira, Marc Giró propone a Pedro Sánchez medidas radicales para España
articles.summary: Entre risas y sátira, Marc Giró propone a Pedro Sánchez medidas radicales para España
articles.body: En un eufórico y satírico monólogo que arrancó entre los aplausos del público, el comunicador Marc Giró dirigió una contundente "carta abierta" al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez. Acompañado por una simulación en plató con la taquígrafa del Congreso, el presentador aconsejó al líder del Ejecutivo sobre cómo afrontar la recta final de la legislatura: "Yo de ti gobernaría estos últimos meses de legislatura siguiendo la máxima de 'por lo que me queda en el convento, me cago dentro' ". Marc Giró instó a Sánchez a posicionarse radicalmente en la izquierda del tablero político: "Gobierna, Pedro, como si estuvieras a la izquierda de la izquierda de la izquierda de la izquierda de la izquierda de la izquierda del PSOE, que es cuanto mejor te ha ido tanto a ti como a la economía española. Cuanto más cabreado tengas a Felipe González, muchísimo mejor". Entre sus recomendaciones más comentadas, el comunicador propuso nombrar nuevos ministerios y estrechar lazos con la oposición de izquierdas para relanzar la estrategia electoral: "Haz ministro a Rufián. ¡Haz ministro a Rufián! Para luego en campaña, cogidos de la mano, liderar juntos el tan cacareado frente de izquierdas". Asimismo, animó al presidente a no ocultar su ideología y su posicionamiento internacional: "¿No eras de izquierdas y propalestina? ¡Pues que se note, Pedro! ¡Que se note!". En el plano territorial, Giró lanzó la propuesta de no conformarse con consultas simbólicas, sugiriendo dar un paso definitivo para contrarrestar a la derecha antes de un eventual cambio de gobierno: "¿Qué coño un referéndum? ¿Para qué andarnos con chiquitas? Lo que hay que hacer antes de acabar la legislatura es dar la independencia a Cataluña, Euskal Herria y a toda comunidad autónoma que lo solicite". Según el presentador, esto desarmaría a sus detractores: "Cuando los fachas lleguen a Moncloa dispuestos, como digo, a desmantelar España, ya se la encontrarán, gracias a ti, bastante desmantelada". El monólogo también abordó en tono cómico la reconfiguración geográfica resultante para los ciudadanos: "Los españoles de bien que queden atrapados en la nueva Fachilandia tendrán la posibilidad de exiliarse a los nuevos países vecinos [...] sin necesidad de saltar a nado a Marruecos, ¡que menuda lata!". Concluyó asegurando que esto inmortalizaría al presidente: "Con esta original medida pasarás a la historia, imagínate la de estatuas ecuestres que se erigirán en tu honor en todas las plazas [...] todas dedicadas a ti: ¡Pedro I, el Libertador!". Finalmente, Giró presentó una batería de medidas económicas de corte revolucionario: "Tengo para ti un paquete de decretos ley inspirados claramente [...] en el asalto al Palacio de Invierno durante la Revolución de Octubre, que pondrán de los nervios a tus opositores, pero muy contentos, muy contentos a los obreros". Recordó que la sigla del partido guarda una clara dirección: "La "O" de las siglas de tu partido no significa ossobuco, significa obrero". articles.title: 'Drishyam 3' advance box office collection: The Ajay Devgn, Tabu film collects Rs 38 crore for the extended opening weekend through advance ticket sales
articles.summary: ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ is set to arrive in theatres tomorrow, October 2, with the Ajay Devgn-led franchise returning for its third and final chapter.
articles.body: ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ is set to arrive in theatres tomorrow, October 2, with the Ajay Devgn-led franchise returning for its third and final chapter. The suspense thriller is releasing as a solo theatrical release on Gandhi Jayanti, giving it the advantage of a national holiday and limited competition at the box office.The film has already generated strong numbers through advance bookings. It has collected nearly Rs 38 crore for the extended opening weekend, including blocked seats, while the figure stands at Rs 28.49 crore when those seats are excluded.For Day 1 alone, ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ has recorded advance bookings worth Rs 19.71 crore. The National Capital Region (NCR) is currently leading the way with Rs 7.76 crore in ticket sales.BookMyShow data indicates that the film is witnessing particularly strong demand in Delhi-NCR, where several shows for the release day are already filling fast. Bengaluru is also showing a similar trend, with multiple shows marked as fast filling. The response in Mumbai and Kolkata appears comparatively slower, while Chennai has shown some encouraging signs.As per industry tracker Sacnilk, the film has sold more than 11 lakh tickets across approximately 36,000 shows, recording an occupancy of 13%. Around 85 shows are already completely sold out. Bollywood Hungama, meanwhile, reported that more than 1 lakh tickets had been sold across PVR INOX and Cinepolis by Tuesday afternoon.The advance booking numbers have already put the third instalment ahead of the opening weekend performance of the first film. ‘Drishyam’ opened at Rs 5.85 crore on its release day in 2015 and earned Rs 37.95 crore during its first weekend.‘Drishyam 2’, released in 2022, witnessed a considerably bigger start, opening at Rs 15.38 crore and collecting Rs 104.66 crore in its first week. The first two films in the franchise have collectively grossed Rs 453 crore worldwide. The third instalment will now attempt to push the franchise's overall global earnings further.With the Gandhi Jayanti holiday providing a boost, trade experts are expecting ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ to register a sizeable opening. Some estimates suggest that the film could even cross the Rs 50 crore mark on its first day.Film trade analyst Sumit Kadel expects the film to open in the Rs 45-55 crore range. “On Day 1, the film might earn between Rs 45 crore to Rs 55 crore. It will mostly depend on how it performs in East India, including Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, as well as in single-screen theatres. The first weekend might easily cross Rs 150 crore,” he said.A strong opening could also see the film challenge Ajay Devgn's existing record for his biggest opener. That record currently belongs to ‘Singham Again’, which opened at Rs 52.20 crore gross, while its net collection on Day 1 stood at Rs 43.50 crore.Film trade analyst Girish Johar, meanwhile, has projected an opening of Rs 35-40 crore, while also highlighting the film's international reach.“The buzz overseas has been great too. In fact, extraordinary,” Johar said, adding, “It is one of the widest overseas releases, with more than 1,300 screens across 60 countries. It is the biggest one for Ajay Devgn.”Ajay Devgn's current highest-grossing film is Rohit Shetty's ‘Singham Again’ (2024), which earned Rs 372.41 crore against a reported budget of Rs 325 crore. The film finished only marginally above its reported breakeven point.The anticipation around ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ also comes at a time when several films have been contributing to an active theatrical market. Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta recently reacted to the theatrical performances of films including ‘Hanuman Ansh’, ‘Awarapan 2’, ‘Mirzapur’, ‘Vvaan’ and the upcoming ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’. Sharing his excitement on X, he wrote, “Much needed happy days at the box office.”With the franchise concluding its story and the benefit of a national holiday, all eyes are now on how ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ translates its impressive advance booking numbers into its actual opening-day collection.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Will 'Hanuman Ansh 2' be made on a budget of Rs 15-20 crore? Producer of the film inspired by Neem Karoli Baba reacts: 'It could even lead to unnecessary use of VFX or AI, which the story may not require'
articles.summary: After the remarkable success of ‘Hanuman Ansh’, producer Anupriya Nagar has said that the makers do not intend to drastically increase the budget for the
articles.body: After the remarkable success of ‘Hanuman Ansh’, producer Anupriya Nagar has said that the makers do not intend to drastically increase the budget for the sequel merely because the first film became a box office hit. According to her, the next chapter will be mounted on a similar scale unless the story itself demands a larger canvas.In a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Anupriya explained that spending more money does not automatically result in a better film and could even compromise the essence of the story."My thinking is very clear: I believe the second film should be made on a budget similar to the first. Simply investing Rs 10 crore or Rs 20 crore would not necessarily make the film better. It could even lead to unnecessary use of VFX or AI, which the story may not require, and that could affect its authenticity."The producer emphasised that recreating the right atmosphere and staying true to the period depicted in the film is more important than increasing production costs."In the period we are depicting, the characters are not the only important element. The landscape, visual texture, atmosphere and the world of that time are equally important. That is why authenticity is our priority."Anupriya also said that the makers are conscious about how they utilise resources, especially after the overwhelming response received by the first film."The audience has given us so much love and support, so we cannot spend money wastefully. Of course, if the next story genuinely requires a larger budget, we will increase it," she said.Addressing the speculation around the film's budget, Anupriya clarified that ‘Hanuman Ansh’ was made on a very modest cost, lower than some reports had suggested."The film was made for slightly more than Rs 1.5 crore, but it was not Rs 2 crore. The budget remained below Rs 2 crore. There are three producers, and each of us contributed one-third of the investment," she said.When asked about the sequel's release plans, Anupriya said it was too early to share a timeline, as discussions on the project are yet to begin in detail."It would be too early to give a definite timeline. Our director has signed another film, so naturally, it will take some time. Our team has not yet had a detailed discussion about the project either. Until that happens, it would not be right to announce a date," Anupriya said.‘Hanuman Ansh’, which released on August 7, emerged as one of the surprise successes of the year, earning praise for its storytelling and strong box office performance despite being made on a limited budget.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: What even is a ‘microdrama’?
articles.summary: Does a vertical recut of the soap opera that made Margot Robbie famous count as a microcrama?
articles.body: On Monday, Variety reported that RoseBerry Media is recutting episodes of the Australian soap opera Neighbours “into microdramas.” These clips will be available on Epis, a short-form vertical video streaming platform. Though Neighbours ran for 41 seasons from 1985 to 2025, at launch, RoseBerry is only recutting two storylines from the late aughts focused on a character played by the now-internationally famous Margot Robbie. In a statement about the project, RoseBerry cofounder / CEO Guy Hameiri described Neighbours as “an iconic piece of television history” that’s well suited to be adapted for vertical viewing with the company’s proprietary, AI-powered production workflow. Hameiri also said that he believes the project will demonstrate how “premium vertical television will become a significant new entertainment category” — one that can help introduce new audiences to a classic series. Variety’s framing of RoseBerry’s new vertical cut of Neighbours as a kind of microdrama is curious. Microdramas are short-form vertical videos often featuring characters who get caught up in convoluted romance plots, which makes them somewhat similar to Neighbours in terms of their shared subject matter. But unlike network television shows with sizable budgets, microdramas are produced on the cheap and crafted specifically to be consumed on mobile. And when you factor in how microdramas tend to adhere to a narrative formula that opens with intrigue and closes on melodramatic cliffhangers, it’s easy to see the format as a storytelling genre unto itself. Over the past year, entertainment trades’ reporting has made it seem like Hollywood is ready to go all in on microdramas, and that these kinds of projects could help the industry bring much-needed production work back to Los Angeles. It’s unclear whether Variety’s phrasing is reflective of the industry’s definition of microdramas changing, or if studios are just trying to use buzzwords to drum up hype. But if microdramas really are going to be a key part of Hollywood’s future, we should probably all have a general understanding of what they actually are. Both the amount of money that went into Neighbours and the quality of the cast’s acting make it a very different kind of entertainment compared to the microdramas that have become hits for companies like ReelShort and DramaBox. What RoseBerry is doing with Neighbours is much more akin to what Tattle TV did with Alfred Hitchcock’s silent film The Lodger: A Story of the London Fog earlier this year, and what startup Snips is doing with series like Big Brother and MasterChef. While there might be an audience for these things, it feels somewhat disingenuous to lump them in with the campy, bite-sized series like Forbidden Fling With My Bestie’s Dad that defined and popularized microdramas as a format in the West. Microdramas originated in China, where they first began gaining traction around 2018 on platforms like Douyin and Kuaishou (both TikTok analogs). Kuaishou’s Unexpectedness — a satirical comedy about a man struggling to achieve his goals — was one of the first Chinese microseries to make a splash, and as the social video platforms embraced e-commerce, brands began to see microdramas as a viable way to market their products to viewers. As the audiences for microdramas grew, more Chinese film / TV production studios began producing microdramas, and by 2021, revenue from short-form video was projected to hit $500 million. That figure was expected to hit $7 billion by 2024 and $16.2 billion by 2030. Though microdramas in all languages tend to be seen as lower-quality entertainment, their core appeal is fairly easy to grasp. The series lean heavily into well-established narrative tropes, and their stories are usually designed to leave viewers guessing about what kind of outlandish twists they’re about to see next. Microdramas’ verticality and the way they’re served up in short minuteslong segments makes them the sort of content that’s meant to be consumed through a phone screen. Microdramas’ relatively small production budgets also positioned them to become a viable way for up-and-coming actors and filmmakers to book consistent work. But in recent months, that promise has been waylaid by the spread of generative artificial intelligence. [Media: In China especially, gen AI has had a devastating impact on the microdrama economy for human actors. Ninety-five percent of the Chinese microdramas produced in the first three months of this year were created with AI, which has led to fewer jobs and lower pay. A similar story is now playing out in Hollywood, where actors have reported being pressured by studios to sign over the rights to their digital likenesses. Though the details are somewhat different, presenting repurposed films and TV series as “microdramas” poses a similar threat to the people working in the business because of the way it cuts them out of opportunities like RoseBerry’s partnership with Epis. It’s also unclear how and whether this new vertical presentation of Neighbours might result in royalty payments to the show’s original cast and crew. Streamers and studios’ interest in vertical content of all kinds has been driven by a desire to recapture some of the attention lost to rival platforms like TikTok and YouTube where microdramas have been able to thrive. For the most part, studios have been leading with repurposed, verticalized clips of preexisting content, which are presented in scrollable feeds that are meant to give you a preview of things that can be watched horizontally. These feeds’ content might be useful for discovery, but very much like microserialized (read: chopped-up) films and TV shows, they aren’t exactly a new entertainment format that seems worth making much noise about. Traditional microdramas haven’t even really had a chance to live up to all the industry hype, but it feels like companies are already rushing to redefine the format as anything that happens to be short, dramatic, and vertically oriented. Platforms might be more interested in turning old shows and films into clip content because it’s less expensive than producing and building an audience for a wholly original microdrama. That doesn’t lend credence to the idea that this format can actually “save” Hollywood, though — if anything, it makes the industry seem like it’s trying to cannibalize itself.

articles.title: Swara Bhasker recalls drunk director knocked at her door and asked her to hug him: 'I was the only woman'
articles.summary: Swara Bhasker has opened up about an uncomfortable experience she allegedly faced with a film director at the beginning of her career.
articles.body: Swara Bhasker has opened up about an uncomfortable experience she allegedly faced with a film director at the beginning of her career. During her stint on ‘Rise and Fall Season 2’, the actress recalled working on a film shortly after ‘Tanu Weds Manu’, in which she played the female lead. She claimed that the director initially sent her messages and poetry before asking her to rehearse a romantic scene with him privately.Speaking to actor Priyanka Chahar Chaudhary and politician Tej Pratap Yadav on ‘Rise and Fall 2’, Swara recalled the circumstances surrounding the film. “This was just after Tanu Weds Manu. It was my big lead film. It was a 56-day shoot. I was the heroine in his film. First, he started explaining to me that, you know, a director should love his actor, this is how it should be. Then he started messaging me. He was sending me poetry," recalled Swara.She said the director later suggested that they rehearse a romantic sequence together. Swara questioned why the rehearsal would involve only the two of them. “Then there was a love scene in a film, like a romantic song. He said we would rehearse this scene. I asked him, ‘Who all are there in this rehearsal?’ He said, ‘You and me, we’ll discuss’," said Swara.The actress said she immediately made it clear that she was not comfortable with the arrangement. “I said, ‘No. You call the actor, you call the camera person. If it is a rehearsal, everyone should do it. Why should we do it alone?’", asked Swara.Swara also recalled the environment at the guest house where the cast and crew were staying. She said she was the only woman there and alleged that the director and cinematographer had already been drinking when she returned to her room.“Where we were staying in the guest house, I was the only woman. I went inside and the director and cinematographer had already finished half a bottle and both were sitting and drinking," she said.According to Swara, the director later came to her room that night and knocked on the door. She said she realised he was drunk when she opened it and that he then asked her for a hug.“Can I get a hug?" he allegedly asked.Recalling her reaction, Swara said, “I was like, ‘No. You cannot get a hug. Please, hug me? What happened? You just want to hug me? I said, ‘No, no, I can’t do it. Sir, please go. I am scared,’" she recalled.Swara suggested that the situation was particularly difficult because she was still a young actor trying to establish herself in the industry. She said the experience left her uncomfortable while navigating the dynamics of working with senior members of a film's team.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: A few days after calling out Govinda and his rumoured girlfriend Komal Rani Swarnkar over their appearance at Lalbaugcha Raja, Divya Khossla has once again addressed the controversy. The actor has now questioned Komal’s sindoor during the religious visit and asked whether she understands the significance attached to the symbol. Divya also urged people not to use religion for personal agendas.The controversy began after Govinda and Komal Rani were spotted at Lalbaugcha Raja on September 22. Several social media users noticed that Komal did not appear to be wearing sindoor when she arrived with Govinda. However, after seeking Bappa’s blessings, she was seen with a red mark around her forehead and hair parting. This led to speculation online about a possible secret wedding between the two.While some netizens interpreted the mark as sindoor, others suggested that it could have been part of the religious rituals at the pandal. One theory doing the rounds was that Komal may have touched her forehead to Bappa’s feet during darshan, which could explain the red mark.Divya, who had earlier spoken in support of Govinda’s wife Sunita Ahuja, has now questioned the way the entire episode unfolded. articles.title: Fiona Lowe, daughter of Chad Lowe and Kim Painter, dies at 13
articles.summary: Fiona Lowe, the daughter of actor Chad Lowe and producer Kim Painter, has died, the family announced.
articles.body: Fiona Lowe, the daughter of actor Chad Lowe and producer Kim Painter, has died, the family announced. She was 13. “We are deeply heartbroken by the loss of our beloved Fiona,” the Lowe family said in a statement posted Wednesday to the Instagram stories of her sister, Mabel Lowe. The family remembered Fiona as “a loving young girl who was smart, creative, and loved to dance.” The statement added: “She was adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents. In fact, she was the light of our lives.” “Her passing is devastating for our entire family and we ask for prayers and privacy at this time,” the family statement said. “If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health, please reach out to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988.” Fiona Lowe’s cause of death was not announced. People was the first outlet to obtain the family statement. Her grandfather, Chuck Lowe, said Wednesday on Instagram: “Rest in peace sweet Fiona.” Born on Nov. 16, 2012, Fiona Lowe was the second of Chad Lowe and Kim Painter’s three daughters. Chad Lowe, an Emmy winning actor with television roles on “Life Goes On” and “ER” who is the brother of actor Rob Lowe, often posted photos of his children on his Instagram page. That included shots of the whole family, pictures of the three girls together and video clips that show the family enjoying their travels and day to day lives. One of his most recent posts of Fiona Lowe featured her on her 13th birthday. “Celebrating Fiona officially becoming a teen today!!” Chad Lowe wrote in the caption. “Keep dancing through life FiBear! Love you soooo much!!” If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline or chat live at 988lifeline.org. You can also visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional support.

articles.title: Michael B. Jordan’s former Hollywood Hills home hits the market for $14 million; Oscar-winning actor bought the four-bedroom LA residence for $5.8 million in 2019; he later sold it for $6.95 million in 2022
articles.summary: Long before Michael B.
articles.body: Long before Michael B. Jordan added an Oscar to his list of accolades for Ryan Coogler’s Sinners, the actor owned a private retreat in Los Angeles’ Hollywood Hills. The four-bedroom residence, tucked away on Woodrow Wilson Drive in Upper Nichols Canyon’s “celebrity row”, is now back on the market, carrying an asking price of $14 million.Jordan acquired the property in an off-market transaction in September 2019 for $5.8 million, according to Mansion Global. He sold it in May 2022 for $6.95 million. The house changed hands again in July 2025, when Joelle Hutner and Jesse Rudolph, founders of design and development studio Ome Dezin, purchased it for $5.25 million.The residence has since undergone an extensive redesign, giving the 1997 property a warmer, more contemporary character while retaining its original architectural identity.A 1990s home with a distinctive architectural characterDesigned by architect Jeffrey Mills, the house was conceived as a meeting point between modernism, brutalism and the softer aesthetic of a French country home. Set across a private acre, the property combines expansive interiors with landscaped outdoor spaces.For Ome Dezin, the existing architecture was not something to be erased but a starting point for the renovation.“The existing architecture and surrounding landscape were the key inspirations for our design direction,” the studio told Robb Report in an email.Hutner and Rudolph, longtime friends who founded Ome Dezin in 2020, have previously worked on the restoration of an original A. Quincy Jones residence in Brentwood and a Tudor-style cottage once owned by burlesque performer Lili St. Cyr.The challenge was making a large space feel intimateThe redesign reportedly took approximately a year and a half. One of the property's defining characteristics, its considerable volume, also presented the designers with their biggest challenge.“The home has a lot of volume and was used as an art gallery before we acquired it, so our biggest challenge was to add warmth, depth, and a sense of intimacy to each space,” Ome Dezin said.Natural colours and materials now run throughout the interiors. In the great room, an asymmetrical brushed stainless-steel fireplace becomes the focal point beneath exposed beams and clerestory windows.The dining room features an integrated wet bar, while the library is anchored by a built-in L-shaped sofa, creating a more relaxed space within the expansive floor plan.A kitchen designed for serious entertainingThe kitchen has been fitted with a La Cornue range and a professional pizza oven, along with a natural stone backsplash. The combination reflects the property's broader design approach, contemporary luxury without completely abandoning the warmth of the original structure.The home includes four bedrooms, five full bathrooms and a powder room. A ground-floor guest suite opens directly onto the pool and gardens.The primary suite features a fireplace, terrace and dressing room, while the adjoining bathroom is particularly striking, with a freestanding marble bathtub and a shower clad in swirling blue-and-white marble.Two additional guest bedrooms each have private bathrooms, balconies and walk-in closets.The backyard comes with a mirrored pavilionThe property's outdoor spaces have been developed as an extension of the interiors. Alongside the swimming pool and spa are a fire-pit lounge, outdoor kitchen and tiered waterfall.One of the most distinctive additions is a cubic pavilion inspired by Doug Aitken's Mirage, the artist's mirror-clad structure in the Southern California desert.Wrapped in reflective material, the pavilion mirrors the surrounding landscape and houses a sauna as well as a chartreuse-tiled bathroom.From $5.8 million to a $14 million asking priceJordan's former home has therefore undergone a notable transformation since his ownership. The actor paid $5.8 million for the property in 2019 and sold it for $6.95 million in 2022. After its subsequent acquisition by Ome Dezin's founders for $5.25 million in 2025, the renovated residence has returned to the market for $14 million.The listing is being handled by Charles Derenne, Silk Fernald and Dominique Madden of the ACME Team at Serhant.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: FOX News Media CEO Suzanne Scott inducted into Broadcasting+Cable Hall of Fame
articles.summary: FOX News Media CEO Suzanne Scott was inducted into the Broadcasting+Cable Hall of Fame on Tuesday, joining innovators, visionaries, and leaders who have shaped the media landscape.
articles.body: FOX News Media CEO Suzanne Scott was inducted into the Broadcasting+Cable Hall of Fame on Tuesday at the famed Ziegfeld Ballroom in New York City, joining innovators, visionaries and leaders who have shaped the media landscape. The annual Broadcasting+Cable Hall of Fame honors behind-the-scenes heavyweights and media stars who have made an unforgettable impact on the industry. Scott, who joined Fox News in its inaugural year of 1996, has risen through the ranks with success at every turn, holding several production and creative positions before taking over as CEO in 2018. Fox News host Bill Hemmer was one of the evening’s emcees, along with ABC’s Will Reeve and CBS’s Vlad Duthiers. Hemmer took the stage to introduce his longtime boss and friend. "Suzanne is the chief executive officer of Fox News Media, which encompasses the Fox News Channel, the Fox Business Network, Fox News Digital, Fox News Audio and Podcasts. And I'm not done, she runs Fox News Books, Fox Nation, Fox Weather and Fox News International. That's a lot of platforms and all of them are a success," Hemmer said. 'THE FIVE' LEADS CABLE NEWS FOR 20TH STRAIGHT QUARTER AS FOX NEWS OUTDRAWS CNN AND MS NOW COMBINED A video tribute to Scott was played, featuring Executive Chair and CEO of Fox Corporation Lachlan Murdoch saying she was the "clear choice" to lead the company and "The Five" co-host Dana Perino saying the decision broke a barrier for women in media. "Suzanne fundamentally understands that we need to be in front of our consumers, she’s done a tremendous job extending our brand to FOX Weather, FOX Nation, our audio business, podcasting as well," Murdoch said. "She doesn’t chase the limelight, she’s not about awards, she’s not about putting herself forward as a celebrity chief executive," Murdoch added. "She keeps her focus on the business and producing the best news and opinion in the entire country, if not in the entire world." Perino added, "I cannot think of anybody in the industry who has loved this business as much as she has. To be No. 1 for 25 years in a row, she makes it look easy." Murdoch and Perino then congratulated Scott, and the FOX News Media CEO took the stage. "I’m so honored to be here. I’m deeply grateful for this honor, the real recognition belongs to my entire Fox News family," Scott told the crowd. "Next month, we will be celebrating our 30th anniversary," she continued. "A very big heartfelt thank you to Rupert and Lachlan Murdoch, two champions of free speech." FOX NEWS MEDIA'S SPOTLIGHT AWARDS CELEBRATE BEHIND-THE-SCENES STARS AS NETWORK NEARS 30 YEARS Under Scott’s leadership, Fox News Channel has dominated cable ratings and regularly beats broadcast networks. Throughout her tenure, all of FOX News Media’s business units have either broken company or industry records while delivering sustained growth. "We have a strong commitment to great storytelling, driving creativity in all of our live broadcasts and adapting all of our businesses as audience consumption happens," Scott said before individually thanking members of the company’s corporate leadership team. "While the talent gets all the attention, equally important is the team behind the camera that no one sees. This recognition tonight belongs to all of them," Scott said. She told FOX News Media President Jay Wallace that the company wouldn’t be where it is without his leadership, told Sean Hannity she was thankful for his loyal friendship and said Chief Foreign Correspondent Trey Yingst represents the network’s dedication to news. FOX NEWS MEDIA EXPANDS PODCAST PORTFOLIO WITH NEW ORIGINAL SHOW ‘THE GIRLS’ "Our goal at Fox News is to meet our audiences where they are," Scott said. "So, we transform the distribution of our content on the traditional and new platforms the audience is engaging with." Scott told the midtown Manhattan crowd that she is a "proud Jersey girl," who comes from a large, diverse family. "I love the Garden State. I actually watched very little TV growing up, and I've been blessed with a loyal, loving, and sometimes really, really loud family debating the issues of the day," Scott said. The FOX News Media CEO ended her speech with a touching moment by thanking her husband, Preston, and daughter Margaux. Fox News personalities Lawrence Jones, Harris Faulkner, Ainsley Earhardt, Trey Yingst, Jessica Tarlov, and Emily Compagno were also among the guests in attendance as Scott was inducted alongside Hemmer, Perino, Hannity, Wallace and other corporate leaders. FIRST LADY MELANIA TRUMP, FOX CORPORATION ANNOUNCE LANDMARK STRATEGIC ALLIANCE TO GROW FOSTERING THE FUTURE Fox News Digital caught up with some of the attendees on the red carpet prior to the event, asking what Scott receiving such an honor means to the network. "She's our leader. When we're looking for direction, or guidance, on what we're doing for that day, or what we do in the future, we look to her, and she's done a terrific job just blazing the trail for all of us," Hemmer said. "She has done a really fantastic job looking toward the future and trying to understand where we’re going," he added. "I applaud her for that." Faulkner said, "It means that someone who is a visionary, who has dreamed for others and for herself, is at the top and leading, right where she should be. I started out in the business when there weren't a lot of women in high places. And I feel like sometimes there are more of us, but she stands alone." Jones said that Scott has been instrumental in his career, saying she has helped him grow over the past decade. "She's the most powerful woman in media, and that comes with trials of its own. She's just now finally getting that acknowledgment from the outside world. Our audience appreciated, our talent appreciated, our chairmen, our ownership appreciated, and now the outside media are starting to give her the flowers that she deserves," Jones told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Scott has created three new streaming offerings, the subscription-based FOX Nation in 2018 and FOX News International in 2020, and FOX Weather in 2021. As part of Scott’s ongoing efforts to expand across platforms, Scott launched FOX News Books in 2020 and also spearheaded the brand refresh of FOX News Digital, FOX News Audio and FOX Business. Bravo’s Andy Cohen, CNN anchor Wolf Blitzer, ESPN’s Stephen A. Smith and Food Network host Bobby Flay were among the other 2026 inductees. articles.title: Netflix chief admits Trump is helping showbiz industry as federal tax credit bill aims to fuel Hollywood jobs
articles.summary: Ted Sarandos praised Donald Trump's push for a federal film tax credit, saying the president "really cares" about creating entertainment industry jobs in America.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — One of Hollywood's top executives offered praise for President Donald Trump as he rallied behind a proposed federal tax credit aimed to bringing back American jobs in the entertainment industry. Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos was asked Wednesday by Bloomberg News' Lucas Shaw what his relationship with Trump is like as the two of them became more acquainted as the streaming giant pursued a buyout of Warner Bros. Discovery, ultimately losing to Paramount. "Well... for everything else you wanna think, he's a guy who really cares about the entertainment business," Sarandos said at the outlet's annual Bloomberg Screentime summit. "And he cares about protecting the industry and creating jobs. And he loves creating jobs in the entertainment business in America." TRUMP CALLS HOLLYWOOD A 'TOTAL DISASTER,' PUSHED FEDERAL TAX INCENTIVE FOR A FILM AFTER MEETING JON VOIGHT In August, Trump expressed support for the federal tax incentive to keep film and television productions within the U.S. versus overseas. Over the past several years, countries like the United Kingdom, Australia and Canada have lured major Hollywood projects using tax credits, and the result was that it could become less expensive to shoot a production across the ocean than to film on the backlot of a legacy studio. The proposed bill, formally introduced last week, has bipartisan support with Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C. and Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., co-sponsoring the legislation. TRUMP, SCHIFF FORGE UNLIKELY ALLIANCE AS HOLLYWOOD BLEEDS JOBS When asked whether he believed the bill will become law, Sarandos expressed some skepticism, citing "a couple of wild card things," such as the result of next month's midterms. "I think it's a bipartisan approach, which helps a lot. I think it's completely sound, and it has a working model that's proven, that you can put a dollar in and get six to nine dollars out, depending on how well you administer the incentive," Sarandos said. "The problem is, is you have, depending on what's going to happen in a couple of weeks, you've got a lame duck session, and if you have a change in control and who wants to champion what, who wants to give you a win. The win for America is if that — if we got it. That would be a win for the country." CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS The Netflix boss dinged Democrat-controlled California for allowing jobs to flee the state over the years. "I just think over the years, California got, I think, complacent that the talent was here. They let the infrastructure age. They make it very difficult to shoot in the city of Los Angeles," Sarandos said. Sarandos continued, "We just finished David Fincher's movie — [it] was no walk in the park. "Animals" ... we shot that in LA. We shot "Cliff Booth" in LA. And we shot the new season of ["Nobody Wants This"]... just those three productions alone — over $400 million in production spending in Los Angeles — without, you know, the best incentives." articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Charlie Sheen: ‘I went from making $2 million a week to making $1,700 a week, and I was never happier. So it ain't about the money,’ a powerful life lesson on happiness, success and finding what really matters
articles.summary: Discover how Charlie Sheen transitioned from earning $2 million per week to $1,700 while finding true happiness. Learn valuable lessons about success and what really matters in life.
articles.body: Money can make life easier, but it does not necessarily make you happier. That can be difficult to remember when success is usually measured by salaries, bigger jobs and the kind of lifestyle that comes with them.Charlie Sheen learned that lesson in a rather unusual way. At the height of his 'Two and a Half Men' career, he was making an enormous amount of money. Then, after losing the sitcom and moving on to another project, his weekly earnings dropped dramatically. Strangely enough, Sheen said he was happier.Today’s quote of the day by Charlie Sheen reads: “I went from making $2 million a week to making $1,700 a week on Roman's film, and I was never happier. So it ain't about the money.”Charlie Sheen said this during a January 9, 2012 Q&A with reporters at the Television Critics Association winter press tour. TheWrap published the conversation under the title 'Charlie Sheen Q&A: What He's Learned in the Last Year'. Sheen was asked what it was like to lose the huge salary he had been earning from 'Two and a Half Men', and he brought up the film 'A Glimpse Inside the Mind of Charles Swan III', directed by Roman Coppola.His answer was not really about pretending money did not matter. He was talking about what he had discovered when the money suddenly became much less important than the work itself.What does the quote by Charlie Sheen mean?Charlie Sheen's point is pretty straightforward: earning more money does not automatically mean you are enjoying your life more.At the time of the interview, Sheen had just gone through a very public split from 'Two and a Half Men'. The show had made him one of television's highest-paid actors, but he had lost the role after his highly publicised conflict with the show's production and network.Then came a much smaller job. Sheen told TheWrap that he went from making millions to earning $1,700 a week on Roman Coppola's film — and said he had never been happier.There is something interesting about that comparison. The number on the pay cheque had gone down, but apparently something else had gone up. For Sheen, at least in that moment, being able to work on something he enjoyed mattered more than earning the biggest possible salary.How is the quote by Charlie Sheen relevant today?It is easy to get caught up in the idea that the next raise, better job or bigger opportunity will automatically make everything better. And sometimes earning more really does make a difference. Financial security matters. But there is more to a good career than the number attached to it.You can have a well-paying job and still hate waking up for it. You can also work on something smaller and find that you actually enjoy your day more. That is what makes Charlie Sheen's answer interesting. He was not saying money is useless. He had experienced what it was like to earn a huge amount of it. He was saying that, after losing that salary, he realised there were other things he valued too.TheWrap's 2012 interview also showed Sheen talking about his new project and wanting to let the work speak for itself. “Just do good work and lead with that,” he said when asked how he would win back people who had turned against him.That part fits with the quote. Sometimes getting back to the work itself can matter more than everything surrounding it.Early life of Charlie SheenCharlie Sheen was born Carlos Irwin Estévez on September 3, 1965, in New York City. He grew up in a family where acting was already a part of everyday life. His father was actor Martin Sheen, while his siblings Emilio Estevez, Ramon Estevez and Renée Estevez also went into acting.Sheen appeared on screen as a child and later started making short films with school friends, including Sean Penn and Rob Lowe. He was expelled from Santa Monica High School shortly before graduation and decided to focus on acting instead.His first major film role came in 'Platoon' in 1986, followed by 'Wall Street' the next year.How did Charlie Sheen rise to fame?'Platoon' was the film that really put Charlie Sheen on the map. It won the Academy Award for Best Picture, while Sheen's performance as Chris Taylor brought him major attention.He went on to appear in films including 'Wall Street', 'Young Guns', 'Major League', 'Hot Shots!' and 'The Three Musketeers'.His biggest television success came with 'Two and a Half Men', where he played Charlie Harper. The sitcom became one of television's biggest shows. Sheen reportedly made around $1.8 million per episode at one point. articles.title: Diddy placed in solitary following NBC News report on his VIP prison life
articles.summary: The disgraced hip-hop mogul has been paying several inmates who do his laundry, make his bed, clean the toilet before he uses it and even give him Chinese-st...
articles.body:
Sean "Diddy" Combs has been placed in solitary confinement following an NBC News report on his VIP lifestyle inside prison, according to a source with knowledge of the matter.

The disgraced hip-hop mogul arrived at the Fort Dix federal prison in New Jersey in October after he was sentenced to 50 months behind bars for transporting people across state lines for sexual encounters.

Since then, he has spent thousands of dollars a month to bring his high-end lifestyle to the low-security prison, NBC News reported Tuesday in a story based on interviews with four men who spent time in the same unit as Combs.

They said he had no trouble acquiring contraband items such as cellphones and premium liquor, including Hennessy. He also pays several inmates who cook special meals for him, clean the toilet and shower areas before he uses them, do his laundry, make his bed and even give him Chinese-style massages.

"This is not some normal s--- you see in jail. This is some rich s---," one of the sources said. "It looks crazy, but again, it's Diddy."

NBC News also obtained photos and videos inside the prison, which include video of Combs appearing to use a contraband cellphone.

After the report was published, Combs was removed from his dormitory-style quarters and placed in a special housing unit, better known as solitary confinement or the SHU, according to the source.

A Bureau of Prisons spokesperson would neither confirm nor deny that Combs was moved.

"For privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not comment on the conditions of confinement for any incarcerated individual, including quarters assignment or whether a particular individual is the subject of allegations, investigations, or sanctions," the spokesperson said.

TMZ was first to report that the Bad Boy Records founder was moved to solitary.

Federal prisons often transfer inmates to the special housing unit when they are the subjects of an investigation, experts say.

"We'd put people in the SHU while we were gathering evidence," said Vito Maraviglia, a retired special investigator for the Bureau of Prisons who worked at Fort Dix in the late 1990s.

Maraviglia said the New Jersey prison is known as one of the cushiest in the federal prison system. It has segmented housing areas that are more difficult to monitor than at other facilities, making it easier for inmates to hide and use contraband items like cellphones.

"A high-profile guy like that, with all that money, I'm surprised they put him at a place like Fort Dix," Maraviglia said.

Inmates placed in the SHU are locked in a cell with one other person for at least 23 hours a day, according to two men who spent time at Fort Dix. Inmates are allowed a book or two and a wind-up radio, the sources said, and they must wear an orange jumpsuit instead of the regular khaki uniform or gray sweatpants and shirts.

Meals are delivered in trays, but commissary access is restricted, and they are permitted to shower only a few days a week. The sources said they must otherwise wash up in a sink.

"It's nasty down there," one of the sources said.

It isn't Combs' first time in solitary confinement at Fort Dix. Last summer, he was placed in the special housing unit after he got into a fight with another inmate.

He was later kicked out of a drug treatment program at the prison but continued paying inmates to do a range of services for him, NBC News reported Tuesday.

The story prompted responses from people as varied as Combs' longtime nemesis 50 Cent and the prominent attorney Gloria Allred, who represents a woman suing him for allegedly raping her more than 20 years ago. (Combs has denied the allegations, and the case is ongoing.)

"These serious allegations against Mr. Combs cry out for an immediate federal investigation and appropriate federal action including a prosecution if the allegations of having and using a cell phone while incarcerated can be proven beyond a reasonable doubt," Allred said in a statement.

Other famous people have also received perks in prison, including Martha Stewart and Harvey Weinstein .

Combs' trial last year centered on drug-fueled orgies he organized called "freak offs." They involved male sex workers and his former girlfriends — including the singer Cassie — who filed a lawsuit against Combs alleging years of physical and sexual abuse. (The case was settled, with Combs denying any wrongdoing.)

The trial ended in a split verdict, with a New York jury finding him not guilty on the more serious charges of sex trafficking and racketeering charges that could have put him in prison for life.

articles.title: El nuevo experimento de Google es un teclado que se mueve y tiene las teclas en una cinta transportadora
articles.standfirst: Eso sí, no está a la venta porque es un proyecto experimental
articles.summary: Eso sí, no está a la venta porque es un proyecto experimental
articles.body: La tecnología avanza a pasos agigantados y Google no va a quedar atrás. Este jueves, 1 de octubre, la compañía ha presentado su nuevo experimento. A tenor de las reacciones en redes sociales, si lo que buscaba era sorprender a sus clientes, lo cierto es que lo ha conseguido. Y es que nunca antes se había visto un teclado en continuo movimiento. Su funcionamiento es fácil de entender, pero te deja boquiabierto nada más verlo. Consiste en un teclado experimental en el que las letras se van acercando a la persona que escribe mediante una cinta transportadora. El usuario debe ser capaz de conectar con la tecla a la vez que ésta se mueve hacia abajo. El dispositivo se denomina Gboard versión Kurukuru. Para entenderlo de una forma más visual. El teclado funciona como una cinta transportadora de los aeropuertos, pero en lugar de llevar maletas, lleva teclas de forma continua. Eso sí, hay que aclarar que no está a la venta, ya que Google considera que se trata de un experimento. Además, se han publicado los códigos y el proyecto para que cualquiera pueda lanzarse a fabricarlo como un proyecto independiente. La compañía ha explicado las razones que le han llevado a configurar un teclado de este modo. Su intención es que ha incorporado esta placa de circuito flexible para permitir escribir con mayor libertad. Las teclas se desplazan hacia las yemas de los dedos, de modo que sea el teclado el que se adapte a las manos y no al revés. De esta forma, Google también valora escribir con una sola mano o con un solo dedo. Hay que destacar que para la compañía, el 1 de octubre se convirtió en la fecha elegida para exhibir diseños experimentales. Éste lo es, pero no ha sido el único que ha visto la luz desde el año 2021.

articles.title: Antoni Daimiel tiene nueva casa tras su adiós de Movistar Plus: RTVE lo ficha para este programa
articles.standfirst: Uno de los rostros visibles del baloncesto y periodismo español llega a la cadena pública
articles.summary: Uno de los rostros visibles del baloncesto y periodismo español llega a la cadena pública
articles.body: Antoni Daimiel ya avisó en su salida de Movistar Plus que tendría ciertas limitaciones a la hora de participar en actividades relacionadas con el baloncesto en televisión. Nadie habló de otros deportes. Tras su salida de la cadena privada, el periodista pasa a formar parte de un programa de RTVE. 'Fútbol de calle', de En Play, ya tiene a su nuevo fichaje. No es la primera vez que el periodista está vinculado con un espacio del deporte rey. Ya ha participado en ‘El día después’, y también la multicámara de los partidos de LaLiga. Eso sí, este espacio de la cadena pública tiene un toque más ‘gamberro’ que los anteriores. Aun así, Daimiel se muestra contento en esta nueva etapa, como bien denotan sus primeras palabras sobre el asunto. A su modo de ver, ‘Fútbol de calle’ tiene “la mirada correcta que considero para el fútbol actual, ya que supone explicarlo, hacerlo entender, entretener, y todo ello con un punto de irreverencia imprescindible”. Hay que recordar que los otros miembros de este proyecto son Pedro El Ingeniero, La Sotanita y Javi Nácher. A pesar de la diferencia de edad, el veterano periodista llega preparado para seguirles el ritmo y unirse a todas las bromas y juegos que le propongan: “Si piensan que el señor mayor viene para ordenar y controlar a los otros tres compañeros, están equivocados. Solo voy a contribuir a alborotarlos más”. Desde RTVE ya han anunciado de forma oficial que se incorpora a ‘Fútbol de calle’ que, a su vez, tiene la intención de “ampliar su contenido futbolístico sin perder su tono humorístico”. En esta segunda temporada, el programa mantiene el formato semanal. Comenzará su emisión a mediados del mes de octubre.

articles.body: Neal McDonough may be known as one of the most ruthless villains in the "Yellowstone" universe, but there's one thing the actor himself has never done: watched the show.
